_comment: Every byte that crosses to the handset, pinned. Engine hashes were read from the actual fabless-pass build output on the build VM (~/workspace/fabless-stack-build/src-llama.cpp/build-android/bin) on 2026-10-28. Model pins were read from the Hugging Face API (sizes + LFS oids; for Git-LFS/Xet repos the LFS oid IS the file sha256) on 2026-10-28. A hash mismatch at setup time is a hard stop, never a warning.

files.name: llama-server
files.role: OpenAI-shaped HTTP server executable (thin launcher) — the seat

files.name: libllama-common.so
files.role: shared common code (chat templates, sampling) — used by both executables

files.name: libmtmd.so
files.role: multimodal support library (linked by the server build; not needed for text-only chat, shipped so the set is complete)

engine.source: llama.cpp cross-compiled by the fabless pass (PR #69), NDK r27c, arm64-v8a, android-28, CPU/NEON backend, shared libs, UNSTRIPPED debug build

model_native_door._comment: The GGUF door of the phone seat. Base model + licence of record live in grok-local's MODEL-MANIFEST.md (Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B, Apache-2.0); the MLC door (browser seat) is pinned there. This manifest pins the native artifact.

alternate_quality.why: Qwen's own official GGUF (Q8_0 only): higher fidelity, ~65% larger, somewhat slower. A config flip in start-server.sh (MODEL_FILE), not a rebuild.

default.why: Q4_K_M at 1.11 GB is the PHONE-ENGINE sweet spot for 6-8 GB phones: fits with room for context, fastest honest class.

server_settings._comment: Phone-seat settings: localhost-only by default (the server has no auth — LAN exposure is an explicit opt-in in start-server.sh), 4K context keeps KV small on 6 GB phones, 4 threads matches the big-core count of both chip classes.
